GenAI: Generative AI is a type of deep learning that focuses on creating new content, such as text, images, audio, video, or code, by learning patterns and structures from existing data - for example DALL-E 3 is the most well-known model used for image creation. Generative AI refers to models that can create new content, such as text, images, or music, based on patterns learned from vast datasets.
LMs - LLMs: Large language models (LLMs) are a form of generative AI that focus on producing text. These foundational models process text token-by-token, enabling everything from creative writing to complex reasoning.
LMs - LLMs - MCP: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, standardizes how applications interact with LLMs—reducing fragmentation, boosting compatibility, and simplifying context management. and it’s essentially a universal connector for AI applications. MCP is poised to become the standard for Al integration. MCP acts as a bridge between reasoning engines (like LLMs) and function executors (like custom APIs). Think of it as the USB-C of the AI world, allowing different AI tools and models to interact seamlessly with various data sources. With MCP, developers can focus on building innovative applications instead of spending time on complex integrations. allowing LLMs to easily access external data and tools, thereby enhancing their capabilities.

AIAgents - Definition: An AI agent is a system designed to reason through complex problems, create actionable plans, and execute these plans using a suite of tools.
AIAgents - LLM: LLMs provide the core reasoning, comprehension, and language generation abilities that agents require.
AIAgents - Types - GoalBased: Goal-Based Agents - Dynamic problem-solvers that adjust actions to achieve specific objectives. Examples include Waymo's self-driving cars and AI-powered project management tools. These agents excel in environments where success metrics are clearly defined but the path to achieve them requires adaptability.
AIAgents - Types - HierarchicalAgents: Hierarchical Agents - Masters of breaking complex tasks into manageable subtasks, like manufacturing robots and air traffic control systems. The structured decision-making approach makes these particularly valuable for mission-critical applications where oversight and predictability are essential.
AIAgents - Types - ModelBasedReflexAgent: Maintaining internal environmental models to make better decisions than simple reactive systems. Think autonomous vehicles predicting traffic patterns or smart thermostats optimizing home environments. Their ability to simulate outcomes before acting creates more sophisticated behavior than purely reactive systems.
AIAgents - Types - UtilityBasedAgents: Utility-Based Agents - Decision-makers optimizing for outcomes by balancing risks and rewards. Financial trading AIs and dynamic pricing systems operate on this principle. These are particularly powerful in domains with quantifiable trade-offs and where optimal decision-making requires weighing multiple competing factors.
AIAgents - Types - LearningAgents: Learning Agents - Self-improving systems that adapt from experience. Fraud detection systems and recommendation engines fall in this category. Their distinguishing feature is the ability to evolve over time, making them increasingly valuable assets that grow more effective with deployment duration.
AIAgents - Types - RoboticAgents: Robotic Agents - The physical manifestation of AI, combining mechanical capabilities with intelligence. Examples include assembly line robots and agricultural harvesting systems. The integration of sensing, processing, and actuation creates autonomous systems that can interact with and manipulate the physical world.
AIAgents - Cycle - Think: The agent processes available data and context.
AIAgents - Cycle - Plan: It decides on a strategy to achieve a goal or answer a question.
AIAgents - Cycle - Act: It executes the chosen plan (e.g., makes an API call, retrieves data, or interfaces with a user).
AIAgents - Cycle - Reflect: It evaluates the outcome of its actions, checks for errors or new insights, and uses those reflections to inform the next iteration of thought. These four steps form a feedback loop that enables agents to adapt their approach as new information arrives.
AIAgents - Features - core: A step up from RAG. Can execute tasks dynamically with minimal intervention.
AIAgents - Features - autonomy: High autonomy adapting to tasks with minimal intervention.
AIAgents - Features - learning: Learn based on agent type and input data.

A2A focuses on how different AI agents talk to each other, no matter which company or framework they come from. It’s like giving AI agents a shared language so they can collaborate, delegate tasks, and work as a team. This is horizontal integration, connecting agents to other agents. creates a unified way for agents to communicate, share data, and delegate tasks—without brittle custom connections.

AgenticAI: Agentic AI is an emerging field that leverages an array of different AI techniques to enable an ‘agent’ to tackle complex tasks autonomously - without human intervention. To do so, it combines the reasoning power of an LLM with an array of tools it can use to perceive and interact with its environment, as well as ML techniques like reinforcement learning. Agents represent the next real step forward in the field of AI
AgenticAI - Features - core: Combines retrieval, generation and dynamic actions.
AgenticAI - Features - autonomy: Very high autonomy combining self-learning and decision making.
AgenticAI - Patterns - Input - SystemInp: Chain-of-Thought (CoT): Forcing the model to explicitly output its step-by-step reasoning tokens (<thought> ... </thought>) before outputting the final answer, which drastically increases logical accuracy.
Few-Shot Prompting Pattern: Providing the AI with 3 to 5 explicit examples of input-output pairs inside the prompt template so it learns the exact format and tone expected of it.

Structured Output Pattern: Enforcing strict JSON schemas or typing on the LLM's response using engineering wrappers, ensuring the output can be parsed safely by traditional code pipelines without crashing.
AgenticAI - Patterns - Execution - ReAct: ReAct (Reason + Act): The foundational agent pattern where an LLM operates in an iterative loop of Thought (reasoning about the problem), Action (calling an external tool or API), and Observation (evaluating the tool's result) until the objective is reached.
AgenticAI - Patterns - Execution - Refle: Reflection / Evaluator-Optimizer: An agent generates an initial draft (e.g., code or a report) and passes it to an evaluator agent. The evaluator critiques the output against predefined constraints and passes feedback back to the generator for iterative self-correction.
AgenticAI - Patterns - Execution - Plann: Planning & Decomposition: Used to solve complex goals by breaking them into structured sub-tasks before executing them. This can be Decomposition-First (building a full roadmap upfront) or Interleaved (planning one step, executing, reflecting, and adjusting).
AgenticAI - Patterns - Execution - Multi: Multi-Agent Coordination: Distributes work across a network of specialized worker agents supervised by a coordinator/orchestrator agent.
Sequential: Agent A finishes its task and passes the output directly to Agent B.
Parallel: Multiple agents process tasks simultaneously, and a coordinator collates the results.
Routing: A cheap, fast model evaluates user intent and dynamically routes the task to a highly specialized, expensive agent.
AgenticAI - Patterns - Control - HumanIn: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL): The AI cannot move to the next step without explicit human intervention or approval. (e.g., A Copilot waiting for you to press Tab).

Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL): The AI operates autonomously through a multi-step process, but a human monitors the live dashboard and can intervene or hit a emergency stop button if it goes off course. (e.g., Devin running tests while you watch the live command line).
Human-out-of-the-Loop (HOOTL): The AI handles the entire lifecycle end-to-end autonomously. Humans only look at the final output after the process is completely finished.
AgenticAI - Examples - SelfDrivingCars: One of the most exciting uses of Agentic AI is in autonomous vehicles. These AI systems perceive their surroundings, make driving decisions, and learn from every trip. Over time, they get better at navigating and handling new challenges on the road. For example, Tesla’s Full Self-Driving system is an example of Agentic AI that continuously learns from the driving environment and adjusts its behavior to improve safety and efficiency.

ContextEngineering - PromptChaining: Prompt chaining, sometimes referred to as Pipeline pattern. Agents receive a series of prompts from the user, with the output of each agent serving as the input for the next in the chain.
ContextEngineering - PromptChaining - 20: Prompt engineering (2022-2024) taught us to communicate with models. Craft better instructions, get better output. But prompts are suggestions. The model can ignore them. There's no enforcement, just hope.
ContextEngineering - PromptChaining - Pr: The information, sentences, or questions that you enter into a Generative AI tool. An AI prompt is the input given to a large language model via a generative AI platform
ContextEngineering - MemoryManagement -: Context engineering (2025) taught us to inform models. Andrej Karpathy championed this: what the model sees matters more than how you ask. Instead of hoping it remembers your coding standards, inject them into context. Real step forward, but the model can still ignore what you show it.
Designing and managing the entire information environment fed into a large language model's (LLM) context window to optimize performance, accuracy, and reliability
AI code churn is the rate at which newly written or AI-generated code is deleted, rewritten, or discarded shortly after being added.

Model collapse is a degenerative process where artificial intelligence models lose quality, diversity, and touch with reality after being trained recursively on synthetic data generated by previous AI models.

When a company switches entirely to an agent-driven development methodology, its human engineers stop reading every line of code; they just look at the high-level summaries.The Result: Over a period of 6 to 12 months, the humans lose their mental model of how the IT system actually processes data.

RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generator) = NLP + LLM. RAG are based on NLP technique to combine rule based output from the LLM itself.

This technique is a step further from LLM making your product more customized based on your requirement (can be dashboards, user stories, etc.) E.g. hashtag#Chatbot hashtag#Midjourney content generators, text to speech converter are a few examples
Limited autonomy with static retrieval and predefined responses.
It does not adapt or learn over time. It retrieves and generates responses based on pre-trained models,

Naïve RAG represents the foundational approach, utilizing straightforward keyword-based retrieval methods like TF-IDF and BM25. While simple to implement, it excels in handling direct, fact-based queries where exact keyword matching is sufficient.

Advanced RAG elevates retrieval capabilities through dense retrieval models like DPR, incorporating neural ranking and multi-hop retrieval. This sophistication enables higher precision and improved contextual understanding, making it particularly effective for complex queries requiring nuanced comprehension.

Modular RAG introduces flexibility through a hybrid approach, combining sparse and dense retrieval methods. Its distinguishing feature is the ability to integrate various tools and APIs while supporting domain-specific pipelines. This adaptability makes it ideal for diverse applications while maintaining scalability.

Graph RAG leverages graph-based structures to enhance contextual understanding. By implementing multi-hop reasoning and node-based contextual enrichment, it excels in relational reasoning and significantly reduces hallucinations. This architecture particularly shines in handling structured data tasks where relationships between information pieces are crucial.

Agentic RAG is a full-blown orchestration layer over RAG. Here, the LLM behaves like an agent — planning, making decisions, analyzing the query, and choosing what tools or strategies to use next. Think of it as an autonomous AI assistant that doesn’t just respond, but thinks and acts. Reasoning loops: “Is this good enough? Should I try another way?” Tool use: From web searches to APIs, agents can leverage multiple sources. Human-in-the-loop: When unsure, agents can ask for clarification. Long-term memory: Learn from past interactions to improve over time. Agentic RAG represents the most autonomous approach, featuring dynamic decision-making capabilities and iterative refinement processes. Through autonomous agents and workflow optimization, it adapts to real-time changes while maintaining high accuracy across multiple domains.
Static content creation, Q&A, and structured knowledge bases.

Self-RAG is a smarter RAG.😎 It introduces self-awareness into the process by grading its own outputs. If the retrieved data isn’t good enough, it rewrites the query and tries again — before even thinking about generating a response. This iterative loop leads to sharper answers and better precision without human oversight. + Adds a layer of validation before generation + Reduces irrelevant answers + Makes LLMs less naive and more cautious + Perfect for ambiguous queries, noisy data, or multi-hop reasoning.
ContextEngineering - HardnessEngineering: Harness engineering (2026) teaches us to constrain models. A custom linter doesn't ask the model to follow the architecture, it rejects code that violates it. A test suite doesn't hope for correct logic, it verifies it. As OpenAI's Codex team put it: Not documented. Enforced.
A harness is the persistent, deterministic structure around an AI coding agent. The harness adds what prompting and context never could: deterministic enforcement.
It has at least one loop with an oracle. Something outside the model decides whether the work is done. Tests, specs, linters, a stress tester, a CI gate. No oracle, not a harness.
It persists. A harness outlives any single prompt. It lives on disk, in the CI config, in the hook scripts, in the spec graph. If it dies when the session ends, it was a prompt.
It enforces rather than suggests. Hooks block. CI rejects. Linters fail the build. Documents the model can ignore are hints, not enforcement.

A skill (the Anthropic SKILL.md pattern) — a capability module the agent loads on demand. Composes into a harness; not one alone.
An MCP server — extends the agent's tool surface. Tools are a layer of a harness, but tools without enforcement or feedback are just a bigger API.
